title: Calgary existing-secondary-suite permit refusal and pre-2018 eligibility dispute (Council Order 2023-02)
jurisdiction: City of Calgary, Alberta (explicitly named as Respondent in the official order, PDF p.1)
code_edition: National Building Code – 2019 Alberta Edition (NBC(AE) 2019), as cited in the order; current-edition applicability is not established by this record

facts.text: The Council order identifies the City of Calgary as the Respondent in an appeal of its refusal to issue a building permit for an existing secondary suite.
facts.locator: PDF p.1, opening matter; p.2, para. 8

facts.text: The official record lists the Notice of Appeal, Council letters, the Appellant Appeal Brief, and the Respondent Appeal Brief; it does not list or append project drawings, photographs, or a separate technical report.

The Appellant’s position as summarized by the order was that the basement contained a pre-March 12, 2018 secondary suite; the order reports the Appellant said a kitchen was installed in 2011 and included a portable cooking utensil, with no kitchen-specific ventilation and no alteration permit.

The order reports that a 2020 building-permit application was first submitted for a new secondary suite, with kitchen development and wall demolition in the scope, and that the City later treated the application as an existing-suite request at the Appellant’s request.

The City’s criteria reproduced in the order required the pre-March 12, 2018 unit to have a sleeping area/bedroom, bathroom, kitchen with a non-portable cooking facility, living area, and a private entrance separate from the main entry; the order also states no fundamental alterations since that date and a signed owner declaration were required.

The Tribunal’s findings describe the earlier basement cooking item as portable and identify post-cutoff wall demolition and kitchen work under the 2020 permit history. These are findings in the appeal order, not independent inspection or drawing evidence attached to this case file.

The order says the City remained available to review a new secondary-suite permit application and that the Tribunal encouraged the parties to complete a new-suite permit path, including alternative solutions where applicable.

limitations: The appeal order redacts the applicant and property identity.
The order is a case-specific appeal decision, not an original application, variance request, or applicant technical report.
The public record list names only party appeal briefs in addition to Council notices; the briefs and project drawings/photos/permit plans are not separately attached to the public decision.
The case cites NBC(AE) 2019, not the current 2023 Alberta Edition.
The order reveals the appeal outcome, so outcome leakage is explicit.
